LESSON: JACOB WRESTLES AN ANGEL

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.5: Jacob Wrestles an Angel

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Jacob Wrestles an Angel. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how they apply lessons learnt in their lives • compose and say a prayer to God. Why is it good to pray always?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify values learnt from the story of Jacob

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: JACOB WRESTLES AN ANGEL
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Jacob Wrestles an Angel helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: JACOB WRESTLES AN ANGEL
Study Jacob Wrestles an Angel like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify values learnt from the story of Jacob

What this means
In this part you learn to identify values learnt from the story of Jacob. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify values learnt from the story of Jacob.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Jacob Wrestles an Angel” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify values learnt from the story of Jacob. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Jacob Wrestles an Angel is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Jacob Wrestles an Angel” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify values learnt from the story of Jacob)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Jacob Wrestles an Angel to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify values learnt from the story of Jacob.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Jacob Wrestles an Angel from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Jacob Wrestles an Angel: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Jacob Wrestles an Angel?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how they apply lessons learnt in their lives • compose and say a prayer to God. Why is it good to pray always?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Jacob Wrestles an Angel means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify values learnt from the story of Jacob.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
